title: 1974: playing in his uncle's church choir
summary: At fifteen he played in Uncle Walter Howard's choir at 8th and San Julian and played a Carl Fischer solo.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: At that time I was 15 years old. I had just graduated from the Steubenville High School, and something like that for a youngster to run into was really difficult, hard to do and hard to work. People were climbing after me and wanting to know what was I going to do here, and all those instruments, play some of them, do this, do that, you know. But
you couldn't always play what you wanted to play. You couldn't always do it.

So my uncle was directing the choir at 8th and San Julian. So I had to skip to the Sunday morning we went to church, and the first thing he did was make me grab hold of my -- the first thing he did was get me to grab -- to get my instruments out and come and go to church and play in the choir, as he was the choir director. And the director of this choir, maybe somebody in Los Angeles might hear this and may know this -- the director of the choir was my uncle. His name was Walter V. Howard, my father's brother. And it was quite a deal to play there on a Sunday morning. Well, me being new, lots of people knew me, because lots of people were here from Ohio and they knew me, and one of the main persons that I met at that time was Mr. Markham. I can't think of his initials right now. It's been too long. 1913's a long time to think, think back to.

But anyhow, I had a very nice reception here at church. I got up and played a solo, and I want to try to think of the name, if these gentlemen will allow me the time to think of the name of the solo I played. And I had -- it was a book -- the book was put out by -- oh, boy -- had all the classics in it. It's a funny thing. Shut it off a minute, Red.
The name of the book was, 'Carl Fischer's Classics,' and it had most all the -- oh, boy. Things leave me too quick. Shut it off a minute, Red.

I played the solo out of a Carl Fischer book, which is something they don't do in churches, applaud, but they applauded me, and I'm trying to think of the name of this piece that I played. It was very beautiful. (Singing). Things like that you don't forget.
We'll get the name on that.

I know what it is. It'll come to me after awhile. But things like that you don't forget and you hum them over and over again, all through your life. And I do certain things, just like I started playing with Isaac McVea's Howdy Band.
